html:
Angkor Thom, "Great City", was the last and longest lasting capital of the Khmer Empire, built in the late 1100s by King Jayavarman VII. Its square wall and moat enclose about 9 square km.

Jayavarman built it after the forces of Champa sacked the earlier capital in 1177 and he drove them out. Five gates lead in, each crowned with giant stone faces, reached by causeways lined with statues of gods and demons pulling a serpent. At the centre stands his state temple, the Bayon. The walled area held the palace, temples and officials; most people lived outside in wooden houses that have vanished.

Older monuments such as the Baphuon stand inside the walls. The Chinese envoy Zhou Daguan visited in 1296 and wrote a vivid account of life in the city. Angkor Thom stayed the capital until the Thais of Ayutthaya attacked in 1431, after which the court moved south toward Phnom Penh. Nearby lie Angkor Wat and the West Baray.
sum: Angkor Thom, "Great City", was the last and longest lasting capital of the Khmer Empire, built in the late 1100s by King Jayavarman VII. Its square wall and moat enclose about 9 square km.
